definitions.explanation: Most commonly refers to thick Japanese-style omelette (厚焼き卵), but can also describe thick-grilled versions of other foods.

examples.japanese: {厚焼|あつや}き{卵|たまご}が{好|す}きです。
このお{寿司屋|すしや}さんの{厚焼|あつや}きは{絶品|ぜっぴん}だ。
examples.english: The thick omelette at this sushi restaurant is superb.

examples.japanese: {厚焼|あつや}き{玉子|たまご}を{上手|じょうず}に{作|つく}るには{練習|れんしゅう}が{必要|ひつよう}だ。
examples.english: You need practice to make a good thick omelette.

notes:
Combines {厚|あつ}い (thick) and {焼|や}き (grilled/baked). Most commonly encountered as {厚焼|あつや}き{卵|たまご}/{厚焼|あつや}き{玉子|たまご}, the thick Japanese-style rolled omelette often served at sushi restaurants. The thick version is distinct from the thinner, sweeter {出汁巻|だしま}き{卵|たまご}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {厚焼|あつや}き{卵|たまご}: thick omelette
- {厚焼|あつや}き{玉子|たまご}: thick egg omelette (alternative kanji)
- {厚焼|あつや}きせんべい: thick rice crackers

RELATED WORDS:
- {卵焼|たまごや}き: Japanese omelette — general term for rolled egg
- {出汁巻|だしま}き{卵|たまご}: dashi-flavored rolled omelette — thinner, Kansai style
- {薄焼|うすや}き: thin-grilled — the opposite, as in thin crêpe-like preparations
